bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar seeks resolution as India's Ganga water sharing treaty with Bangladesh expires this year
bihar_raw_news.content: The Ganga enters Bihar’s Buxar district and flows 445 km before entering West Bengal. | Afzal Adeeb Khan via Mongabay. As the Ganga water-sharing treaty between India and Bangladesh ends this year, Bihar seeks to resolve its long-standing demands before the treaty is renewed. The treaty, signed in December 1996, governs the sharing of the Ganga river’s water between upstream India and downstream Bangladesh, particularly during the lean season when river flows are low. Under the treaty, during the lean period from January to June, if water at the Farakka barrage is less than 70,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs), India and Bangladesh each get half. If the water at the barrage is between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs, Bangladesh will be assured 35,000 cusecs, and the rest will go to India. If the water is 75,000 cusecs or more, India will get an assured 40,000 cusecs, and Bangladesh will get the rest. The agreement further says Bangladesh will get a guaranteed flow of 35,000 cusecs on the first and last ten days of April and 27,633 cusecs between April 11 and 20. If the Ganga’s flow falls below 50,000 cusecs in any ten-day period, the two governments will enter immediate consultations to make emergency adjustments. For decades, Bihar’s political leaders have argued that the Ganga water-sharing treaty with Bangladesh does not adequately account for the state’s water needs. Sanjay Jha, a member of parliament from Bihar’s ruling party Janata Dal United, said on August 6 during the Zero Hour in Rajya Sabha that renewing the treaty without adequately incorporating Bihar’s long-term water security, development needs, and water resource requirements would harm the state’s broader interests. He further said that adequate availability of Ganga water is essential for Bihar’s agriculture, drinking water supply, industrial development and long-term water security, all of which depend on the Ganga basin. People assemble at Ganga ghat in Patna, Bihar. Image by Afzal Adeeb Khan via Mongabay. Bihar government’s claim Citing the data of second Bihar State Irrigation Commission report , prepared in 1994, two years before the Ganga water-sharing treaty was signed, Bihar government said in 1997 that the state has only about 16% of the Ganga’s total catchment area. Still, the state has to provide half of the water the Farakka Barrage needs during the lean period, and it gets this water from the Ganga’s tributaries that flow through the state. Around a dozen rivers in Bihar join the Ganga, according to the Bihar disaster management department. In December 2017, the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation had organised the Vision Ganga programme, where Rajiv Ranjan Singh, the then water resource minister of Bihar, now a Union Minister, had said that at the entry point of the Ganga river in Bihar near Buxar district, the flow is only 14,126 cusecs. bihar_raw_news.title: 'Today I only see denuded land': Mango orchards give way to Adani's power plant
bihar_raw_news.content: In Bihar’s Bhagalpur district, a 2,400 MW thermal power plant is rising on land whose true costs are only beginning to surface. Awarded to Adani Power Ltd in a Rs 30,000 crore deal, the Pirpainti project has moved forward through disputed compensation, broken promises, and a public hearing farmers say was engineered to silence them. The two-part series traces what has been erased in the process. The first part examines how hundreds of farmers across 12 villages have watched their orchards vanish without adequate compensation for either land or their orchards. The second turns to a community left out of the process entirely: two Santhal and Pahariya Adivasi hamlets sitting within the project site itself, absent from official lists of affected communities — left with no guaranteed right to compensation or rehabilitation. Adani Power rejected any suggestion of legal or regulatory violations, saying the Pirpainti project is fully compliant and that it supports local communities and jobs. *** On the morning of February 19, Sushil Kumar walked out of a meeting with government officials believing his land and trees would remain safe for 15 days. The 49-year-old was among a group of farmers in Bihar’s Bhagalpur who had gathered for a high-level meeting, attended by officials of district administration, the police and the state’s Energy Department. They wanted permission from the farmers to cut 100 trees to build a road to a 2400 MW thermal power plant being built by Adani Power. The meeting went on from 11:30 am to 12:45 pm at the end of which a clear agreement was reached: no work would take place on the disputed land for the next 15 days. The farmers, who had to rush for another hearing, for which they were served notices on the same morning, left with some relief. The notices were served under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which permits an executive magistrate to take preventive action to maintain public order. It wanted them to appear before the official and furnish a bond of Rs 1 lakh each. While they were occupied with the hearing, the promise given to them in the morning was broken, allegedly by district administration officials who arrived at the site along with a contractor. “They brought a JCB machine, illegally felled seven mature trees, and stole the timber,” Sushil wrote in a police complaint he filed afterward. Sushil’s land lies in Pirpainti block, on the southern banks of Ganga River and barely 30 kilometres from the 2340 MW Kahalgaon Super Thermal Power Station. His land is now on the site of a second, larger power project – a 2,400 MW ultra-supercritical thermal plant, backed by a Rs 30,000 crore investment, awarded to Adani Power Ltd (APL), on the land allotted by the Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited (BSPGCL). bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Approves Raiyati Land Purchase Policy 2026 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Approves Raiyati Land Purchase Policy 2026 28 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar government has approved the Bihar Raiyati Land Purchase Policy 2026 to facilitate the purchase of private land for public projects through mutual consent, offering higher compensation and additional incentives to landowners. Key Points Financial Compensation & Incentives: Landowners will receive compensation of up to four times the higher of the market value or circle rate in rural areas and twice that value in urban areas. Landowners will receive an additional 10% incentive , and eligible transactions will be exempt from stamp duty and registration fees. Transactions conducted through this mutual consent framework are fully exempt from stamp duty and registration charges . Mutual Consent & Conflict Reduction: The policy enables mutual-consent land purchases for public projects, including roads, bridges, railways and hospitals, to reduce delays and disputes. Farmers are being informed about the three land procurement options to facilitate informed decisions and land assembly for urban development projects. Approval Mechanism: Projects (estimated value of land to be purchased) worth up to ₹100 crore will be decided by a committee headed by the District Magistrate; larger projects will be handled by a committee chaired by the Divisional Commissioner. Three Land Procurement Options: The government can use mutual-consent purchases, direct land acquisition or land pooling. Under land pooling, 55% of the pooled land will be returned to owners in a developed form. Progress: The Urban Development and Housing Department has initiated discussions with farmers for proposed satellite townships in Pataliputra (Patna) and Gaya . bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR–MGIFRI, Motihari Organizes Soil Health Awareness Programme for Climate-Resilient ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 28 October 2026, Motihari, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organized a soil health awareness and field assessment programme under Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA) – Rabi 2026 at Sangrampur Chaur, East Champaran, Bihar, today. The programme focused on soil health management, balanced fertilization, flood-induced crop damage assessment and climate-resilient farming practices in waterlogged rice-growing ecosystems. The programme was organized under the overall guidance of Dr Raghavendra Singh, Director, ICAR–MGIFRI, who emphasized the importance of developing location-specific, climate-resilient farming strategies for flood-prone and waterlogged areas of Bihar. He highlighted the need for scientific soil health management, efficient nutrient utilization, crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices to improve farm productivity and strengthen farmers' livelihoods. The field programme involved field observations, soil sampling, and farmer interactions to assess soil health and crop management challenges under varying waterlogging conditions. Fields were classified into three categories: uplands with minimal waterlogging, intermediate Chaur fields with 3–5 days of waterlogging, and low-lying Chaur fields with 13–15 days of water stagnation. The programme highlighted the effects of flooding on rice growth, crop recovery, and subsequent Rabi crop establishment, emphasizing timely crop planning, improved drainage, suitable crop selection, and climate-resilient practices. Technical guidance was also provided on soil testing, balanced fertilizer application, integrated nutrient management, and organic resource recycling to restore soil health and sustain crop productivity. During the interactive session, farmers shared their experiences regarding water stagnation, rice crop damage, soil fertility deterioration and difficulties in cultivating low-lying fields. The scientific team provided practical guidance on soil health improvement, nutrient management, crop diversification and location-specific Rabi crop planning. The programme strengthened soil health awareness, farmer–scientist interaction and climate-resilient agricultural planning in flood-prone Chaur ecosystems. The initiative reaffirmed ICAR–MGIFRI's commitment to promoting healthy soils, balanced fertilization, sustainable crop management and resilient farming systems under Khet Bachao Abhiyan – Rabi 2026, particularly for small and marginal farmers in the waterlogged regions of eastern India. A total of 23 farmers participated and interacted with the scientific team regarding soil fertility constraints, seasonal flooding and sustainable crop management. (Source: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar)

bihar_raw_news.title: Nashik: Bihar Delegation Visits Zilla Parishad To Study Maharashtra's Panchayati Raj System
bihar_raw_news.content: Nashik: A delegation from the Government of Bihar visited the Nashik Zilla Parishad on Wednesday to study the functioning of Panchayati Raj institutions in Maharashtra, their administrative structure and various aspects of the financial empowerment of local self-government bodies. During the visit, the delegation gathered information on the administrative and political framework of the Zilla Parishad, its internal revenue sources, the functioning of various departments and the overall office management system. The delegation included Naveen Kumar Singh (IAS), Director of the Panchayati Raj Department, Additional Secretaries Mohammad Wasim Ahmed and Amritesh Kumar, Under Secretary Shubham and Prabhash Chandra Jha from the PM-CB/BSPRI unit. Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer Omkar Pawar welcomed the delegation and provided a detailed overview of its operations. He briefed the officials on various development initiatives implemented in rural areas through the Zilla Parishad, Panchayat Samitis and Gram Panchayats, as well as the functioning of the administrative machinery. Read Also Nashik: ₹9.20 Crore Ramkal Path Project To Restore Historic Wadas, Temples Along Godavari Focus on Internal Revenue Sources Discussions during the visit centred on the financial self-reliance of Zilla Parishads. The focus remained on internal revenue sources, opportunities for increasing income, financial planning and the process of fund allocation. The delegation also inquired about coordination between the administrative and political wings of Panchayati Raj institutions, the responsibilities of different departments and the execution of development projects by local self-government bodies. The delegation visited various departments within the Zilla Parishad office to observe day-to-day administrative operations firsthand. The officials also sought information on department-specific responsibilities, operational procedures and the overall administrative structure. Read Also Nashik: ₹26,839 Crore Mobility Plan Proposes Light Metro, 1,339 More Buses And New Roads Studying Operational Practices Through Exchange of Experiences The primary objective of the visit was to conduct a comparative study of the functioning of Panchayati Raj institutions in Maharashtra and Bihar, understand the characteristics of their administrative systems and gain insights into various aspects of local self-governance. Such study tours enable Panchayati Raj institutions from different states to benefit from each other's experiences and identify effective practices to improve their administrative processes. Zilla Parishad Deputy Chief Executive Officer Mahesh Patil and Chief Accounts and Finance Officer Maruti Mule were also present. They provided the delegation with detailed information on relevant administrative and financial matters.

bihar_raw_news.title: Book on Bihar's Development, Political Leadership Launched at PCI in Delhi
bihar_raw_news.content: Last Updated on October 28, 2026 6:14 pm by INDIAN AWAAZ By Wasi Imam / NEW DELHI Bihar’s development challenges, governance priorities and the role of political leadership in shaping the state’s future came into focus at the launch of The Advent of a Statesman: Bihar Has Never Had It So Good , authored by journalist and columnist Gyan Bhadra, at the Press Club of India in New Delhi on October 25. The book was unveiled during the three-day Literature Festival and Book Fair organised by the Press Club of India from October 24 to 26. Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty, festival convenor and president of the Press Club of India, formally launched the publication in the presence of journalists, publishers and members of the media fraternity. Veteran journalist Gautam Lahiri, president of the Federation of Press Clubs and former president of the Press Club of India, was among those present. The launch was followed by a panel discussion examining the book’s arguments on Bihar’s development trajectory, political leadership and governance. Abhay N. Jha, an independent journalist and former special correspondent of the Assamese daily Asomiya Pratidin , was the chief panellist. The discussion addressed some of Bihar’s longstanding socio-economic challenges, including declining educational standards, inadequate healthcare infrastructure, agricultural distress, rural hardship, migration and the difficulties confronting women in rural areas. These concerns framed a broader debate on the state’s development priorities and the effectiveness of political leadership in addressing structural problems. A key question raised during the discussion was whether the book’s title, The Advent of a Statesman , presented an overly optimistic assessment of Bihar’s political leadership. Panellists also questioned whether a single leader could bring about a fundamental transformation in a state grappling with complex and deeply rooted challenges. Responding to these questions, Bhadra explained that the title reflected the perspective advanced in his book. He maintained that an assessment of Bihar’s progress must consider both the changes achieved and the challenges that remain unresolved. On the question of leadership, Bhadra stressed that sustainable development could not be the achievement of one individual alone. While political leadership could set priorities, mobilise public support and guide institutional processes, lasting change required effective administration, sound economic policies, private investment, civil society participation and active citizen engagement. He argued that the relationship between political leadership and institutional capacity was particularly important for Bihar, where improvements in education, healthcare, agriculture, employment and rural livelihoods demand sustained and coordinated efforts. The discussion moved beyond an assessment of an individual leader to examine the wider questions of institutional reform, inclusive growth and governance. It also highlighted the need to evaluate political promises against tangible improvements in people’s lives. The event provided a platform for journalists and readers to engage with the book’s arguments and debate the opportunities and challenges that will shape Bihar’s developmental future.

national_raw_news.title: Sports, Education Ministries and UNESCO sign MoU to take clean sport values to every classroom 14 mins ago 3
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’. The MoU was exchanged in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis. Addressing the event, Mr joshi said that the MoU would help address the longstanding gap between education and sports. He also said that students who performed well academically did not always participate in sports, and emphasised the need to strengthen grassroots opportunities and build better pathways for young athletes. Meanwhile, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya said that sporting excellence and sporting integrity must go hand in hand. He added that talent, discipline and hard work are essential for sporting success, but integrity, fairness and credibility are equally important. The initiative is aimed at embedding values such as respect, integrity and fairness in children through education, sports and everyday classroom activities. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the toolkit’s video modules will be made available in 13 Indian languages, with the objective of reaching students across the country and building a stronger, fairer sporting ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: Cabinet approves scheme worth Rs 10,000 cr to promote domestic manufacturing
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to promote domestic manufacturing.The total outlay for the scheme is ten thousand crore rupees for 13 years upto Financial Year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units. He said, it has four components including Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification assistance, Land Leasing support and Operational Expenditure Assistance. Mr Vaishnaw added that the scheme will create an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme will strengthen resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains. It will generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. The Union Cabinet has also approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods. Giving details about the scheme , Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that that the scheme has an approved outlay of over one thousand 856 crore rupees over eight years period from 2026-27 to 2033-34. He said, the scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India’s position in global supply chains. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems. Mr Vaishnaw added that incentives and interventions are the two parts of the scheme where incentive supports manufacturing while intervetion builds the wider ecosystem. The Union Minister also said that a key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth. Mr Vaishnaw also informed that the Union Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PMVGSY) scheme as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. It aims to transform Panchayats into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. Mr Vaishnaw said that the scheme has a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees and the duration of the scheme is for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. He said, the scheme applies to all States and Union Territories, including rural local governance institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist. It will cover more than 2.78 lakh Rural Local Bodies and Traditional Bodies across the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. Mr Vaishnaw informed that Union Cabinet also approved three percent increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July,2026. Mr Vaishnaw added that this will benefit over 48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners. The combined impact on the exchequer on account of increase in both Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief would be over 10,000 crore rupees per annum.

national_raw_news.title: EAM S Jaishankar to attend G20 FMs’ meeting this week: MEA
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar will be attending the G 20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Atlanta, US from 30th to 31st October. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that on the sidelines, Dr Jaishankar will also participate in a QUAD Foreign Ministers Meeting. He will also have several bilateral engagements with his counterparts. Mr Jaiswal informed that from Atlanta, the External Affairs Minister will travel to St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda to lead the Indian delegation for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting to be held from 1st to 4th November. The theme of the forthcoming CHOGM is “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”. Regarding FATF meeting underway in Paris, the spokesperson said that India’s stand is amply clear as far as terror financing and cross border terrorism is concerned. He said terror financing and cross border terrorism need to be held accountable. He further stated that the world needs to do more so that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations can be fought harder and defeated by the global community. On energy sourcing, the spokesperson said it is based on national interest. He pointed out that energy sourcing is done by the companies, which take into consideration commercial conditions that are available, market conditions at that point of time as also the global situation. Replying to a query on SCO Civilisational Civilizational Dialogue Forum meeting, Mr Jaiswal said India has invited all SCO members as per established practice. He said India has also invited dialogue partners and one observer to the SCO. He added that they have been invited to the Civilizational Dialogue Forum meeting, which will be held in New Delhi from 20th to 22nd November. On West Asia conflict, the spokesperson expressed India’s deep concern about the ongoing conflict in the region. He informed that 22 Indian nationals have died in the conflict, including 14 seafarers. He said India remains in close touch with the community in the Gulf region for their safety and well-being. He said that three Indians have lost their lives in Saudi Arabia. Replying to a query on Northeast and Japan, Mr Jaiswal asserted that India has strong partnership with Japan. He further stated that several intiatives are underway involving Northeast and Japan. He said New Delhi would like to further these linkages. He said work is going on to further strengthen India Japan economic technology partnership, and in that larger rubric, Northeast is also getting attention.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi says, India must embrace emerging technologies and lead world in creating them
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. The Prime Minister stated that the nation is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor technology. He highlighted that just a few months ago, the 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor successfully achieved first criticality. Mr Modi said that science truly succeeds when it steps out of the lab, improves the lives of common citizens, solves massive problems, and strengthens healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience. He also highlighted that over the past year, the government has committed 12 thousand crore rupees to market-ready lab technologies, matched equally by 12 thousand crore rupees from private investors. He noted that annual patent filings have grown from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a deeper structural shift beyond mere numbers. Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies. He highlighted that the India of the 21st Century is moving ahead with a new mindset and newfound confidence. He stated that the goal is to create new technology for India, for the world, for today, and for the days to come. Meanwhile, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh has said that India has established its position in science, innovation and technological capabilities, and the world is looking at the country with respect and admiration. He added that the international conference is witnessing enthusiastic participation, with thousands of experts and delegates joining the event on Indian soil. Prime Minister Modi also visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.

national_raw_news.title: India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions: S...
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya has said that India will bring further amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions. He said the move is aimed at strengthening action against doping violations, including those involving coaches and supply chain stakeholders. Dr Mandaviya made the announcement while chairing the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026-27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi. The Minister said sporting excellence must be accompanied by integrity and that athletes should compete on the basis of talent, preparation and hard work, rather than prohibited substances or methods. Highlighting the country’s efforts to combat doping, Dr Mandaviya said India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026. He said the government plans to bring another amendment in the next session of Parliament to introduce criminal provisions to deal more effectively with violations, including those involving coaches and stakeholders in the supply chain. Dr. Mandaviya said the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) conducted more than 7,000 tests during 2025-26 and organised over 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching approximately 27,000 participants. The agency has also focused on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations to strengthen its efforts against doping.

national_raw_news.title: UAE President honours FlyDubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with top civilian bravery award for s...
national_raw_news.content: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on the flydubai crew members, including Captain Smit Machchhar. The honour, one of the UAE’s top civilian awards, has been conferred in recognition of their courageous efforts to ensure the safety of passengers during an in-flight incident aboard FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. The UAE President, in the presence of Vice President & Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, received the crew members. The leaders praised the crew’s courage and professionalism in ensuring the safety of passengers and securing the aircraft, affirming that protecting people’s safety and security remains a top priority for the UAE. The crew members expressed their gratitude to the UAE President and pride in receiving the honour, which reflects recognition of their service, dedication and commitment. The honours were presented by UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, who commended the crew’s actions and sense of responsibility. The ceremony was also attended by Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, and Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of Dubai Airports and Emirates Airline and Group, along with other senior officials. On September 30, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot while aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 enroute from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The crew, assisted by another pilot on board and passengers, intervened to bring the situation under control. The pilots regained control of the aircraft and diverted it to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely. UAE investigations later revealed that the co-pilot had planned to seize the aircraft and carry out an attack at Tel Aviv airport.

national_raw_news.title: Exit polls show deadlock in Israeli Parliamentary elections, setting stage for coalition government
national_raw_news.content: The parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament – Knesset. The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail. Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later. With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government.

national_raw_news.content: The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Kakinada. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the landfall process started at 1:20 AM today. The crossing began earlier than originally expected due to the rapid movement of the storm. The storm hit the coast, packing sustained maximum wind speeds of 115-125 km per hour, with gusts reaching up to 140 km per hour. Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted normal life across several coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh. In Puducherry, normal life has been affected in the coastal region of Yanam as cyclonic storm Arnab began making landfall near Kakinada in the early hours of this morning. Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Continuous rainfall since last night has affected Ranchi and several other parts of Jharkhand due to Cyclone Arnab. The Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall and strong winds. The West Bengal administration has stepped up precautionary measures in view of Cyclonic Storm Arnab. According to the Alipore Meteorological Office, scattered rainfall is likely in several districts of West Bengal today. Isolated spells of heavy rain are forecast in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, and Jhargram. Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri in North Bengal may also experience rainfall accompanied by gusty winds.

national_raw_news.content: Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Southern Odisha continues to experience heavy rain and strong winds under the influence of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which is crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. According to the India Meteorological Department’s latest available landfall update, the storm was centred near the Andhra coast, close to Narsapur, after moving west-north-westwards. It is crossing the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam, with sustained wind speeds of 125 to 135 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 145 kilometres per hour. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur are among the districts facing severe weather. Gopalpur recorded the highest rainfall in the state over the last 24 hours, according to the available information. No casualties have been reported in Odisha so far. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and the Revenue Minister scheduled to review post-landfall developments at the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Authorities have shifted more than one lakh people living in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A number of trains have been cancelled, or routes have been diverted for today, while bus services to southern districts from other parts of the state have been completely suspended. Fishing activities remain suspended as the sea continues to be very rough.

national_raw_news.title: Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people
national_raw_news.content: Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people: Vaishnaw Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Mobile PLI scheme generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct taxes, employs 12 lakh people: Vaishnaw ANI | Updated: Oct 28, 2026 07:51 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 28 (ANI): The government's mobile phone production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme has generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections against an incentive payout of Rs 19,000 crore, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said, highlighting the financial returns and employment generated by India's mobile manufacturing sector. In a post on X on Wednesday, Vaishnaw said the government had paid Rs 19,000 crore in incentives under the mobile PLI scheme, while direct tax collections stood at Rs 25,000 crore and Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections at Rs 3,000 crore. "Electronics manufacturing employs 25 Lakh people; mobile manufacturing alone employs 12 Lakh," the minister said. His remarks came as he refuted a news report questioning the effectiveness of India's mobile manufacturing model and the role of government incentives in the sector. The figures shared by the minister come as the government seeks to expand domestic mobile phone manufacturing, increase local sourcing of components and strengthen India's position in global supply chains. In July, the Union Cabinet approved the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) with a budgetary outlay of Rs 62,500 crore. The scheme, which will run from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, aims to scale up production, deepen domestic value addition, strengthen supply chains and improve global competitiveness. The scheme provides incentives ranging from 2.25 per cent to 5 per cent for eligible mobile phone sales, with an additional incentive of up to 1.5 per cent linked to domestic sourcing of key components and sub-assemblies. It also provides support for Indian mobile brands, including incentives linked to design and research and development. According to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, cumulative mobile phone production during the scheme's tenure is expected to reach approximately Rs 39 lakh crore, with a significant increase in exports. The scheme is also expected to generate around 60,000 direct jobs. The new scheme follows the end of the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing on March 31, 2026, as the government looks to sustain manufacturing growth while encouraging deeper domestic sourcing and Indian-owned brands. national_raw_news.content: India's Rs 38,000 Crore Thoothukudi Mega Shipyard Project Advances As Sonowal Meets HD Hyundai Chairman In Seoul Infrastructure India's Rs 38,000 Crore Thoothukudi Mega Shipyard Project Advances As Sonowal Meets HD Hyundai Chairman In Seoul Swarajya Staff Oct 28, 2026 | Updated 03:35 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal today (28 October) met HD Hyundai Chairman Chung Ki-sun in Seoul to advance India's proposed greenfield shipyard at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. The meeting took place during Sonowal's four-day visit to South Korea, focused on deepening bilateral cooperation in shipbuilding and the wider maritime industry. HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE), the shipbuilding arm of HD Hyundai, reiterated its intent to participate as a primary strategic investor in the project. A joint working group will now oversee project development, while the two sides work towards agreeing a joint venture structure. The Detailed Project Report is expected to be finalised within six months. The proposed shipyard is envisaged to have an annual capacity of approximately 2.5 million Gross Tonnage, with the project valued at around Rs 38,000 crore or roughly $4 billion. Once operational, it is expected to become India's largest commercial shipyard, significantly strengthening domestic shipbuilding capacity and the country's competitiveness in the global maritime industry. The initiative builds upon a tripartite memorandum of understanding that was signed on 20 April 2026 between HD KSOE, National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Tamil Nadu Limited, and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited. The project forms part of the India-Republic of Korea comprehensive framework for partnership in shipbuilding, shipping and maritime logistics. The facility is planned as the anchor for the Thoothukudi Shipbuilding Cluster being developed by NSHIP-TN, with the techno-economic feasibility report already completed. The yard is expected to generate approximately 15,000 direct jobs once operations stabilise, with further employment across supporting industries in Tamil Nadu. The project aligns with India's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, which targets annual shipbuilding output of 4.5 million GT by 2047. national_raw_news.title: India, Mexico launch preferential trade agreement talks to expand trade, investment
national_raw_news.content: India, Mexico launch preferential trade agreement talks to expand trade, investment Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India, Mexico launch preferential trade agreement talks to expand trade, investment ANI | Updated: Oct 28, 2026 11:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 28 (ANI): India and Mexico have formally launched negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), setting a framework to expand bilateral trade, attract investment and strengthen supply chains, as the two countries seek to deepen economic cooperation across key sectors. The negotiations began with the signing of the Terms of Reference (ToR) by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal and Mexico's Undersecretary of Foreign Trade Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The ToR lays down the framework, scope, modalities and roadmap for negotiations. The proposed agreement aims to create new business opportunities and promote investment flows through balanced and mutually beneficial terms. India and Mexico agreed to deepen their partnership following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025. The negotiating framework covers market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, dispute settlement, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade and trade remedies. The ministry said the proposed agreement would seek to use complementarities between the two economies and expand opportunities for Mexican products and businesses in the Indian market. Mexico's links with global value chains also make it an important market for Indian exporters and investors, it added. Sectors identified for potential cooperation include automobiles, chemicals, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, energy, critical minerals, medical devices and advanced manufacturing. The Indian and Mexican delegations also discussed opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties and promote closer cooperation between businesses in both countries. In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Mexico said the signing marked “a decisive step towards a stronger economic partnership”. “Our shared ambition: expand trade, unlock investment, strengthen supply chains and create new opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the embassy said. The embassy added that both countries were ready to turn untapped potential into tangible economic benefits through “balanced, ambitious and mutually beneficial negotiations”. The two sides also discussed the possibility of organising a Mexican business mission to India in the first quarter of 2027. The proposed mission would facilitate business-to-business meetings, identify commercial opportunities and strengthen commercial ties between businesses in both countries. The negotiations will now provide a framework for the two sides to work towards a preferential trade agreement and identify areas where closer economic engagement can translate into concrete business opportunities. Bilateral trade data showed that India-Mexico trade stood at USD 7.83 billion in 2025-26, down 9.11 per cent from USD 8.62 billion in 2024-25. India's exports to Mexico declined marginally by 0.38 per cent to USD 5.73 billion, while imports fell 26.59 per cent to USD 2.11 billion.
